Each panel is drawn with `eigenplot!`: the eigenvalues of one matrix (points), the ellipse that
`elliptic_law` predicts from the moments of its off-diagonal pairs (line), the predicted outlier
from a nonzero mean where there is one (open circle), and the stability boundary `Re λ = 0`
(dashed). The cases follow chapter 4 of Allesina's
*Theoretical Community Ecology* notes; `test/elliptic_law.jl` checks the same cases. Rebuild with
`just gallery`.

```{julia}
using FoodWebs, CairoMakie
using Distributions: Normal
using LinearAlgebra: eigvals
using Random: Xoshiro
using Statistics: mean
using Printf: @sprintf

# off-diagonal pairs zero with probability 1 - C, otherwise with mean μ, variance σ² and
# correlation ρ, from normal or uniform marginals
function sparse_pairs(rng, S, C, d; σ = 1.0, ρ = 0.0, μ = 0.0, uniform = false)
    M = zeros(S, S)
    draw() = uniform ? sqrt(12) * (rand(rng) - 0.5) : randn(rng)
    for i in 1:(S - 1), j in (i + 1):S
        rand(rng) < C || continue
        z1, z2 = draw(), draw()
        M[i, j] = μ + σ * z1
        M[j, i] = μ + σ * (ρ * z1 + sqrt(1 - ρ^2) * z2)
    end
    M[CartesianIndex.(1:S, 1:S)] .= d
    return M
end

# the mean matrix of a matrix whose upper and lower triangles have different means
function triangle_means(J)
    S = size(J, 1)
    upper = mean(J[i, j] for i in 1:S for j in (i + 1):S)
    lower = mean(J[i, j] for j in 1:S for i in (j + 1):S)
    return [i < j ? upper : i > j ? lower : 0.0 for i in 1:S, j in 1:S]
end

fmt(x) = @sprintf("%.2f", x)
nothing
```

## May's matrices

Off-diagonal entries are zero with probability `1 - C` and otherwise have mean zero and variance
`σ²`. The eigenvalues fill a disc of radius `√(SCσ²)` around the diagonal value, whatever the
distribution of the entries (May 1972; the circular law). Here `S = 500`, `C = 0.2`, `σ = 1`,
so the radius is 10.

```{julia}
rng = Xoshiro(1)
fig = Figure(size = (900, 450))
for (k, uniform) in enumerate((false, true))
    ax = Axis(fig[1, k]; title = uniform ? "uniform entries" : "normal entries", xlabel = "Re λ", ylabel = "Im λ")
    eigenplot!(ax, sparse_pairs(rng, 500, 0.2, -10.0; uniform))
end
fig
```

## Interaction types

With pair correlation `ρ` the disc stretches to an ellipse with semi-axes `√(SCσ²)(1 ± ρ)`
(Sommers et al. 1988). Predator–prey pairs have opposite signs and `ρ < 0`, so their spectra are
narrower along the real axis and their matrices are easier to stabilize than those of
competition or mutualism, with `ρ > 0` (Allesina & Tang 2012).

```{julia}
fig = Figure(size = (1200, 450))
for (k, ρ) in enumerate((-0.5, 0.0, 0.5))
    ax = Axis(fig[1, k]; title = "ρ = $ρ", xlabel = "Re λ", ylabel = "Im λ")
    eigenplot!(ax, sparse_pairs(rng, 500, 0.2, -10.0; ρ))
    limits!(ax, -27, 7, -17, 17)
end
fig
```

`random_predprey` pairs a negative entry `-|a|` with a positive entry `f |b|`, with `a` and `b`
independent normals. With `f = 1` the pair correlation is `-E|a| E|b| / E[a²] = -2/π ≈ -0.64`
and the mean is zero; with `f < 1` the mean is negative and adds an outlier on the stable side.

```{julia}
web = may_network(rng, 400, 0.1)
fig = Figure(size = (900, 450))
for (k, f) in enumerate((1.0, 0.3))
    J = random_predprey(rng, web, Normal(), f)
    sol = elliptic_law(J)
    ax = Axis(fig[1, k]; title = "f = $f: ρ = $(fmt(sol.ρ)), outlier at $(isnan(sol.outlier) ? "none" : fmt(sol.outlier))",
        xlabel = "Re λ", ylabel = "Im λ")
    eigenplot!(ax, J)
end
fig
```

## Outliers from a nonzero mean

A mean `μ` of the off-diagonal entries adds the rank-one matrix `μ(11ᵀ - I)`, with eigenvalue
`θ = (S - 1)μ`. When `|θ|` exceeds the radius `√(Sσ²)` it appears as an outlier, shifted by the
pair correlation to `θ + ρSσ²/θ` from the center (O'Rourke & Renfrew 2014). Without the
correction the prediction is off by `ρSσ²/θ`, here about 1.4.

```{julia}
fig = Figure(size = (900, 450))
for (k, ρ) in enumerate((0.0, 0.5))
    M = sparse_pairs(rng, 500, 0.2, -5.0; ρ, μ = 0.5)
    sol = elliptic_law(M)
    observed = maximum(real, eigvals(M))
    ax = Axis(fig[1, k]; title = "ρ = $ρ: outlier $(fmt(observed)), predicted $(fmt(sol.outlier)), uncorrected $(fmt(sol.μ_diag + (sol.S - 1) * sol.μ))",
        xlabel = "Re λ", ylabel = "Im λ")
    eigenplot!(ax, M)
end
fig
```

## Structured food webs

The elliptic law assumes the pairs are exchangeable: any pair of entries is as likely to hold the
predator's effect above the diagonal as below. Food web models break this. In a cascade web,
species eat only lower-ranked species, so every predator's negative effect lies above the
diagonal and every prey's positive effect below. The mean matrix then has one constant in each
triangle, and its eigenvalues (crosses) are large and nearly imaginary. They predict the
imaginary extent of the cascade spectrum, which reaches several times the ellipse.

The shuffled panels are a null model, not a food web. `shuffle_prey = true` keeps which pairs of
species interact and the sizes of their effects, but flips a coin for which one of each pair is
the predator, so about half the links point down the hierarchy and the web has no consistent
direction of energy flow. That makes the two triangles statistically alike, which is what the
elliptic law assumes, and the spectrum fills the ellipse. Comparing the two columns isolates
what the trophic hierarchy itself does to the spectrum.

The niche model only partly follows this: its imaginary extent goes beyond even the
triangle-mean prediction, and its spectral abscissa beyond the bulk. In the niche model the
probability of a link depends on the species' niche values, so the mean structure varies within
each triangle. Allesina et al. (2015) study the stability of these structured webs.

```{julia}
S = 400
fig = Figure(size = (1100, 900))
rows = []
for (r, (name, gen)) in enumerate((("cascade", cascade_network), ("niche", niche_network)))
    w = gen(rng, S, 0.1)
    for (c, shuffle) in enumerate((false, true))
        J = random_predprey(rng, w, Normal(), 1.0; shuffle_prey = shuffle)
        means = eigvals(triangle_means(J))
        ax = Axis(fig[r, c]; title = "$name, $(shuffle ? "shuffled" : "structured")", xlabel = "Re λ", ylabel = "Im λ")
        eigenplot!(ax, J)
        shuffle || scatter!(ax, real.(means), imag.(means); marker = :xcross, markersize = 9, color = :darkorange)
        sol, λ = elliptic_law(J), eigvals(J)
        push!(rows, (name, shuffle, maximum(imag, λ), sol.y_semi_axis, maximum(imag, means), maximum(real, λ) + 1, sol.x_semi_axis))
    end
end
fig
```

```{julia}
#| output: asis
println("| Web | Pairs | Max Im λ | Ellipse Im semi-axis | Triangle-mean max Im | Max Re λ − d | Ellipse Re semi-axis |")
println("|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|")
for (name, shuffle, im, y, m, re, x) in rows
    println("| $name | $(shuffle ? "shuffled" : "structured") | ", join(fmt.((im, y, m, re, x)), " | "), " |")
end
```

## References

- May, R. M. Will a large complex system be stable? Nature 238, 413–414 (1972).
- Sommers, H. J., Crisanti, A., Sompolinsky, H. & Stein, Y. Spectrum of large random asymmetric
  matrices. Phys. Rev. Lett. 60, 1895–1898 (1988).
- Allesina, S. & Tang, S. Stability criteria for complex ecosystems. Nature 483, 205–208 (2012).
- O'Rourke, S. & Renfrew, D. Low rank perturbations of large elliptic random matrices.
  Electron. J. Probab. 19, 1–65 (2014).
- Allesina, S. et al. Predicting the stability of large structured food webs. Nat. Commun. 6,
  7842 (2015).
- Allesina, S. Theoretical Community Ecology, chapter 4,
  <https://github.com/StefanoAllesina/Theoretical_Community_Ecology>.
